sum: China's Shanghai Composite inched higher on Monday 9 November 2026, with coal miners, aircraft makers and physical AI concepts offsetting weakness in lithium and solar names, as softer domestic inflation data and reports of an extended US-China trade truce met a sharp drop in trading activity.

The Shanghai Stock Exchange Composite Index closed at 3,660.79 on Monday 9 November 2026, up 11.61 points or 0.32% from Friday's close of 3,649.18. The modest gain recovered part of Friday's 1.10% decline, which had come at the end of a week in which the index rose 1.39% overall and broke a run of six consecutive weekly losses.

Monday's performance was mixed beneath the surface. While the Shanghai benchmark advanced, the Shenzhen Component Index and the start-up focused ChiNext Index each fell 0.27%, and more than 3,100 stocks across both exchanges finished lower. The large-cap CSI 300 barely moved, adding 0.05% to 4,056.11, while the tech-focused STAR Composite gained 0.44%.

Chinese equities opened higher as technology stocks rebounded in line with the rest of Asia, following a recovery in US chip shares late last week. The early rally lost momentum through the session, however, as investors digested official data showing consumer inflation decelerated in October, a reminder that domestic demand remains soft despite Beijing's support measures.

Investors also weighed the global backdrop. The weekend news that Nvidia's board had opened an investigation into chief executive Jensen Huang, whose relationship with an executive reportedly linked by US officials to Chinese intelligence has been dismissed by Beijing as a smear, added a layer of geopolitical uncertainty around the technology sector. At the same time, Italian financial press reported during the European session that China had extended its trade truce with the United States by two months, a development that, if confirmed, would remove a near-term source of tension ahead of a 10 November deadline on rare-earth export controls.

Coal producers were the standout performers. China Coal Energy rose 3.33% and Shaanxi Coal and Chemical Industry gained 2.79%, with Zhengzhou Coal Industry and Electric Power and Yunmei Energy also among the leaders.

sum: Mainland Chinese stocks opened higher but slid in the afternoon as optical-module and circuit-board makers sold off on Nvidia’s leadership turmoil, while banks hit record highs and kept the Shanghai benchmark well ahead of Shenzhen.

The Shanghai Composite Index closed at 3,634.35 points on Friday 13 November 2026, down 21.48 points or 0.59%. It was the index’s second straight decline after a 0.67% fall to 3,655.83 on Thursday, and it left the benchmark back below its five-day and ten-day moving averages. The session range ran from 3,623.84 to 3,669.44.

The headline loss understates the damage across the wider market. The Shenzhen Component Index fell 2.05% to 10,968.79, the growth-focused ChiNext Index slid 3.32% to 2,426.08, the STAR 50 lost 2.30% to 1,279.66 and the blue-chip CSI 300 eased 0.68% to 4,016.29. More than 4,700 stocks declined against roughly 750 that rose, and combined Shanghai and Shenzhen turnover shrank to about 1.66 trillion yuan, around 276 billion yuan less than on Thursday.

A-shares opened higher and the Shanghai Composite traded in positive territory through the morning, briefly rising about 0.2% towards 3,663. The tone changed sharply after the lunch break, when selling hit the computing-hardware complex and the index fell almost 1% at its worst before trimming losses into the close.

The dominant story of the session was the abrupt exit of Jensen Huang, the co-founder who had led Nvidia since 1993. The company said on Thursday that he had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member with immediate effect, following reports of multiple affairs, including one with a woman US intelligence suspects of spying for China. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, Harvey C. Jones becomes the company’s first independent chairman, and Nvidia is due to report quarterly results next week. Nvidia shares opened as much as 14% lower on Thursday before closing down 4.34%, and extended losses on Friday after HSBC downgraded the stock.

Chinese suppliers of optical modules, printed circuit boards and electronic components have been among the biggest beneficiaries of US AI data-centre spending, so the uncertainty around Nvidia’s strategy hit them hardest.

sum: On Nov. 13, China's three major A-share indexes diverged, with the ChiNext Index and Shenzhen Component Index opening higher in the morning before steadily declining, while the STAR 50 at one point rose more than 2% intraday before pulling back. At the close, the Shanghai Composite Index was down 0.59%, the Shenzhen Component Index down 2.05% and the ChiNext Index down 3.32%, with more than 4,700 stocks across the market closing lower.

On the trading front, combined turnover on the Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses was 1.66 trillion yuan for the full day, down 276.4 billion yuan (approximately $41.4 billion) from the previous session, a clear contraction in volume. The market showed pronounced structural characteristics: heavyweight and thematic stocks each had their moments, but growth sectors came under broad pressure.

The areas that bucked the trend were concentrated in AI animated drama and banks. In the AI animated-drama theme, Wintime Holding notched its fourth limit-up in five days, Jinyi Cinema posted its second limit-up in four days, Happy Blue Ocean surged 20% to its daily cap, and Hengdian Film & Television and Hubei Radio and Television also closed limit-up. Bank stocks were active, with Bank of Jiangsu, Bank of Nanjing, Bank of Qingdao, Bank of Chengdu and Bank of Hangzhou all hitting record highs. In addition, Tianpu, part of the computing-power chip theme, recorded a fourth straight limit-up, Huadong Heavy Machinery hit its cap, and pork names moved: Jinxinnong and Tianbang Food both closed limit-up.

On the downside, computing-hardware shares fell broadly, led by CPO and PCB names: Kinwong Electronic hit the limit-down, while TFC Communication, Yuanjie Technology and Eoptolink Technology all weakened. This segment had previously been a focus of market fund flows, and the day's pullback was a clear drag on the ChiNext Index.

Looking at the intraday rhythm, the STAR 50 at one point climbed more than 2% in the morning but failed to hold its gains, and index losses widened in the afternoon, reflecting that funds chose to take profits at high levels.

sum: On Nov. 12, China's three major A-share indexes rallied before reversing course. The ChiNext Index rose nearly 2% intraday, then turned lower in the afternoon and extended its losses to close down 2.44%. The Shenzhen Component Index fell 1.68% and the Shanghai Composite Index lost 0.67%. More than 4,600 stocks across the market closed lower in a broad-based selloff.

Turnover on the Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses totaled about 1.93 trillion yuan (approximately $289.5 billion) for the full day, up 255.8 billion yuan (approximately $38.4 billion) from the previous session.

Sector performance was sharply mixed. The gas sector strengthened repeatedly, with Dongfang Huanyu posting a fourth consecutive limit-up and Hongtong Gas hitting the daily limit. Consumer stocks also showed gains, with Guangzhou Grandbuy, Ningbo Zhongbai, Haodangjia and Huifa Food all closing limit-up.

On the losing side, precious metals names weakened, with Shanjin International, Chifeng Gold, Western Region Gold and Shandong Gold all falling. The AI comic-drama concept swung lower: Shanghai Film closed limit-down, Huace Film & TV dropped more than 10% and Wentou Holdings reversed into negative territory after briefly hitting the limit-up. Robotics and physical-AI concepts declined, with Fulai New Materials among those closing limit-down.

sum: Equity market indices are expected to witness a positive opening on Monday, November 9, as indicated by the GIFT NIFTY futures, with investors focusing on steady crude oil prices and US Treasury yields, the momentum from Asian markets, and the overall FII buying this month.

The equity futures were indicating a positive performance for the trading session on Monday's market, as investors focused on the buying momentum from the Asian markets. NSE data showed that the NIFTY50 index slipped under the 25,000 mark to end 0.18% or 43 points lower at 24,986.40 points after the Muhurat trading session on Sunday, in comparison to 25,030.35 points at the previous stock market close.
The BSE SENSEX ended 0.04% or 28.62 points lower at 80,999.40 points on November 8, in comparison to 81,028.02 points at the previous stock market close, according to the exchange data.

While FIIs sold for the first time in six days, the selling streak of domestic investors was maintained for the seventh consecutive trading session on Sunday, November 8.

sum: China’s central bank and securities regulator are expected to meet with financial institutions on Monday to discuss measures to bolster the country’s stock market, following a sell-off in October that heightened concerns over market stability, according to mainland media reports.

The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) will meet representatives from major banks alongside the National Financial Regulatory Administration and the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) to discuss measures to optimise a lending facility designed to support share buy-backs and stake increases by listed Chinese companies and their major shareholders, state-owned Shanghai Securities News reported on Sunday, citing industry sources.

Some securities firms and fund managers received notices of a meeting with the PBOC and CSRC scheduled for Monday to discuss the use of policy tools aimed at supporting the capital market, according to the report.

NEW YORK (AP) — The bond market swung Wednesday, while U.S. stocks ticked higher following the Federal Reserve ’s decision not to raise its main interest rate to bring down high inflation. The S&P 500 rose 0.3% after drifting between small gains and losses through the day, both before and after the Fed’s decision. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 97 points, or 0.2%, and the Nasdaq composite rose 0.3%.

The action was much stronger in the bond market, where the yield on the two-year Treasury initially climbed after the Fed announced it was holding the federal funds rate steady. It got above 4.79% from 4.70% late Tuesday after the Fed said two officials actually wanted to raise the fed funds rate, only to get outvoted by their peers.

The central bank last month raised its main interest rate for the first time in three years in hopes of bringing down inflation, which has remained above the Fed’s 2% target for years and has been discouraging Americans broadly.

But the two-year Treasury yield, which closely tracks expectations for Fed action, quickly reversed course. It dropped as low as 4.69% after Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said the central bank wanted to see how conditions play out before making its next move.

He pointed to how rates for loans have climbed and how lenders and investors have become “more discerning.” He said the overwhelming judgment among Fed officials at their meeting was that “monetary medicine” is “starting to work some.”

items.t: MSCI keeps South Korea as emerging market, delays Indonesia review amid downgrade risk
sum: Index provider MSCI kept South Korea classified as an "emerging market" in its most recent review on Tuesday, while extending its assessment of Indonesia's status until November.
The decision dashed hopes that Seoul could be included in MSCI's Developed Markets watchlist, a crucial step before a market can be upgraded to developed-market status.

For Indonesia, the extended review comes after MSCI raised concerns about market accessibility earlier this year and froze the country's stocks from its indexes in January, citing investability concerns.

MSCI said that it would continue evaluating reforms introduced by Indonesian authorities, but should these measures prove insufficient, the index provider would "consider a range of options for the appropriate treatment for the Indonesia market," including a potential downgrade to frontier-market status.

Following the review, Indonesia's financial regulator reportedly said that it would "ensure that the reforms that have been and are currently being rolled out can be comprehensively understood by the global investment community."
In South Korea's case, MSCI said limited convertibility of the Korean won in the offshore currency markets remained a key barrier to reclassification.

The index provider also cited a rigid investor identification system, restrictions on in-kind transfers and off-exchange transactions, and limits on investment products due to restrictions governing the use of exchange data.

items.t: How China uses a ‘national team’ to influence trading
sum: Beijing sees a stable, steadily rising stock market as essential to the country’s economic transition

[BEIJING] China’s stock market has long been more volatile than Beijing would like, a problem that has taken on greater urgency as the government tries to shift growth away from property and debt and towards technology and innovation.
Equities are increasingly expected to help fund companies, support household balance sheets and reinforce confidence at a time of intensifying economic pressure and strategic rivalry with the US.

That helps explain why authorities, amid a strong January rally that stirred fears of speculative excess, leaned on a state-backed “national team” to influence trading – a reminder of how closely share prices are intertwined with China’s broader economic and political objectives.
Why does the government want to control China’s stock market?

In order for this strategy to work, however, China must prevent the boom-bust cycles that have plagued its stock market. The epic crashes of 2007 and 2015 have since deterred many retail investors from the market. Their contribution and behaviour are important; with 240 million retail traders in China, they make up around 60 per cent of daily trading. Goldman Sachs estimates that as of mid-2025, around 11 per cent of household wealth lay in equities and mutual funds.

Beijing also wants to entice institutional investors – such as pension funds and insurers – and their long-term capital into the market. For these reasons, authorities are willing to cushion losses during periods of market panic and temper excess during rallies, using its so-called national team to intervene.

sum: Dongfeng Motor Group is a broad-based Chinese automaker with operations spanning passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, engines, components and related services. An Eulerpool analysis describes the group as headquartered in Wuhan and active in vehicle development, production, marketing and servicing.

The group serves passenger-car and commercial-vehicle markets and also produces engines, transmissions, axles and other parts. Its portfolio includes internal-combustion, hybrid and battery-electric vehicles, giving the business exposure to the shift toward lower-emission transport while retaining established vehicle operations.

Dongfeng also works through joint ventures and partnerships with international manufacturers, including Nissan, Honda and Peugeot-Citroen, according to the analysis. Those relationships support technology sharing and extend the group's reach across China's highly competitive automotive market.

Dongfeng competes with GAC Group, Geely Automobile and Great Wall Motor. The company stands out through its combination of passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and component manufacturing, while more specialized rivals focus more heavily on selected passenger-car or new-energy segments.

The breadth of the portfolio can diversify operating exposure, but it also places Dongfeng across several businesses with different demand cycles and technology requirements. For investors, progress in electric vehicles, overseas expansion and the performance of joint ventures remain important areas to watch.

Dongfeng Motor Group is headquartered in China and manufactures and sells vehicles, engines, components, spare parts and related services. Its main markets are China and selected international markets, with business lines covering passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, engines and components. The group is broader than the named competitors in product scope, while its position in China reflects scale and established partnerships rather than a single-vehicle niche.

sum: Mainland stocks ended higher, rebounding from a two-month low on Tuesday, as tech shares led gains on signs of easing geopolitical tensions and as global markets shrugged off worries that the AI sector is overheating.
In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended trading on Tuesday up 178 points, or 0.69 percent, at 25,894.
Shares of Alibaba were up HK$3.30, or 2.13 percent, at HK$157.80 ahead of its earnings later in the day, which could affect sentiment among Chinese tech companies.
Shares of Xiaomi closed HK$1.68, or 4.4 percent, up at HK$40.34 after its founder and chairman, Lei Jun, bought shares in the open market.

Tech majors traded in Hong Kong rose 1.2 percent, following an overnight rally in their counterparts traded in New York. The index is down nearly 20 percent from a four-year peak hit in early October.
Investors have been taking profits on most days this month in sectors that have rallied strongly in 2025, including technology and innovative drugs.

items.t: Morgan Stanley predicts moderate gains in China stocks in 2026
sum: Morgan Stanley predicts mild gains in China stocks in 2026 as blistering rally cools
First call by a Wall Street bank predicts gains between 3.4 and 4.6 per cent from current levels for gauges including the Hang Seng Index
China’s stocks will post moderate gains in 2026, maintaining momentum after a torrid run-up that placed them among the world’s best performers this year, according to Morgan Stanley.

The MSCI China Index, a gauge of the nation’s major companies trading both domestically and overseas, could finish at 90 by the end of next year, implying a 3.4 per cent gain from its current level, analysts led by Laura Wang at the US investment bank said in a report over the weekend.

Morgan Stanley said its year-end target for the Hang Seng Index was 27,500 and that for the CSI 300 Index of Chinese onshore stock was 4,840, suggesting gains of 3.5 per cent and 4.6 per cent, respectively, from current levels.

items.t: Asian shares fall, tracking Wall Street’s tumble on worries about AI stocks and interest rates
sum: Currency traders watch monitors near a screen showing the Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) at the foreign exchange dealing room of the Hana Bank headquarters in Seoul, South Korea, Nov. 14, 2025. (AP Photo)

MANILA--Asian shares retreated on Friday, tracking Wall Street’s tumble to one of its worst days since April as Nvidia and other AI superstar stocks kept dropping on worries their prices have shot too high.
South Korea’s Kospi led the regional decline, falling 3.2% to 4,038.61 amid the global tech sell-off. Samsung Electronics shed 4.1% and SK Hynix was down 6.4%. LG Energy Solutions gave up 3.7%.
Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell nearly 1.7% to 50,438.99, reversing the previous day’s gains. SoftBank Group led the slide, plunging 5.7% amid losses in its technology and AI related investments.
In Chinese markets, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index shed 1.3% to 26,732.99, while the Shanghai Composite index slipped nearly 0.2% to 4,022.89.

Data on Friday showed China’s factory output grew at a 14-month low of 4.9% year-on-year in October, down from 6.5% in September and below expectations of 5.5%. Investment in fixed asset such as factory equipment also fell 1.7% year-on-year in the January to October period.
Persisting weakness in property investments were a key factor dragging on business investment.
